actual_checks: Read the actual arXiv1408.5794v2 header and Theorem5/equation0.5, whose critical-line exponent is13/84+epsilon. The separate mean-value result is not confused with this theorem; no latest-record claim is made.

F=(s-1)/(s+2)*zeta is holomorphic on the enlarged right strip, and its boundary bounds have polynomial growth. The real part of the affine L interpolates the exponents. On vertical boundaries, ((|t|+2)/(|t0|+2))^a exp(-(t-t0)^2) is bounded uniformly in t0 for a>=0. Horizontal edges vanish for fixed t0; removal of the rational factor is uniform for |t0|>=2.

The interpolation line at delta,eta->0 is2theta(1-sigma); losses can be chosen uniformly over sigma. Functional equation gives1/2-sigma+2theta*sigma=1/2-(29/42)sigma for the left half, continuous at sigma=1/2.

Small fixed-radius Cauchy disks fit an enlarged pole-free strip at large height; the continuous piecewise-linear exponent is Lipschitz. Radius and intermediate epsilon losses are fixed before height, giving constants depending on j,epsilon and uniformity in sigma. No growing-order derivative estimate is claimed.
Lindelof yields the stated replacement exponent by the same reasoning with arbitrary eta, and j=0,sigma=1/2 recovers precisely its pointwise quantifiers.
